shipped_rows.title_o: Detecting the Snake in the Grass
shipped_rows.outcome_quote: Overall, participants were not significantly faster at detecting threatening stimuli. Thus, results were not supportive of the hypothesis that visual detection of evolutionarily relevant threat stimuli is enhanced in young children. (...) The current crowdsourced replication project was an attempt to replicate a finding from LoBue and DeLoache (2008), Experiment 3, as well as to test for moderation of this effect by protocol (RP:P vs. revised). Although we observed some trends in the expected direction— the participants were faster to detect threatening, compared with nonthreatening, stimuli—the effect size was considerably smaller than in the original study and did not reach statistical significance.
